clue.text: Deal with ring-leader in meeting

indicators.note: in tells us the leading letter goes inside the word for a meeting

parts.note: a meeting between people is a contact

indicators.note: the leader of ring is its opening letter, the one at the front

explanation.surface: Someone negotiates with the ringleader of a gang during a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring-leader' looks like the gang boss, but it splits: the leader of 'ring' is R, which goes in CONTACT.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract is a formal agreement, the same thing as a business deal.

clue.text: Some money of equal value to rest

definitions.meaning: coins handed back or small coins in general
from the proverb that a ... is as good as a rest

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition leans on the British saying 'a change is as good as a rest'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coins in the pocket are change; and a change of scene is, proverbially, as good as a rest.

clue.text: Unsettled type in section of church holding it up

indicators.note: holding says the word for a church section contains the other piece

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word it is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A drifter sits in part of the church and holds up the service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unsettled' does not mean restless: a native was there before any settlers arrived. In a down clue 'up' turns the word it upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A native belongs to a place by birth, an original inhabitant rather than an incoming settler.

clue.text: He provides relations with nothing in a current arrangement

indicators.note: in places the letter for nothing among the other letters
an arrangement of letters puts them into a new order

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A man supplies his family members with nothing as part of a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relations' looks like family, but means accounts or stories. O goes with A CURRENT, and 'arrangement' shuffles them.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a skilled storyteller, one who relates anecdotes.

clue.text: Settles misunderstanding, and so improves the atmosphere

definitions.meaning: removes confusion or ill feeling by talking openly
literally freshens the weather or the room

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means ending tension by frank discussion; literally, a storm freshens the sky.

clue.text: Dwelling with artificial thatch taking heavy blow, we hear

parts.note: thatch is slang for hair, so artificial hair is a wig

indicators.note: we hear says the next word is to be taken by its sound when spoken

parts.note: a wham is a heavy, resounding blow

explanation.surface: A hut with a fake thatched roof takes a battering in a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' joins the pieces. WHAM said out loud gives WAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A wigwam is a domed hut of some Native American peoples, a kind of home.

clue.text: One of the Romans had taken over old state

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken over says the word had is flipped and read upward

explanation.surface: A Roman citizen took control of an ancient state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One of the Romans' looks like a person, but it is the Roman numeral I. 'taken over' reverses HAD to DAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty US states.

clue.text: Cosmetic treatment isn't commonly provided after distortion -

indicators.note: after puts the slang word for isn't behind the word for distortion

parts.note: a warp is a twist or distortion
ain't is the common, colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A beauty treatment goes wrong when the face is distorted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided' is only a link; 'after' sets the slang form behind the distortion.
explanation.definitionFit: War paint is jokingly used for heavy make-up, a cosmetic application.

clue.text: A thousand turkeys cooked for old soldiers

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

indicators.note: cooked means falsified or messed about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thousand turkeys are roasted to feed retired soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' in the sense of fiddled, as with accounts, tells you to rearrange the birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Musketry once meant a body of musket-armed troops, soldiers of an earlier age.

clue.text: Things Anthea has collected

definitions.meaning: the name Anthea is made up of A, N, THE and A, so it has gathered up grammatical words of that class: an, the, a

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a joke: the name Anthea is a collection of 'an', 'the' and 'a', which are the articles of English grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: Objects or items are called articles; and a, an and the are the grammatical articles.

clue.text: Sign he's got out of reference book

indicators.note: got out of says the letters of he's are taken out of the longer word

parts.note: a thesaurus is a reference book of synonyms
he's gives its letters without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone looks up a star sign after taking it from a reference book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got out of' tells you to take HES out of THESAURUS, which leaves T and AURUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Taurus, the Bull, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Jumping over crowd where race begins

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first word above the second

parts.note: starting means jumping in surprise
the gate is the crowd attending a sporting event

explanation.surface: Horses leap over the spectators at the start of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gate' for the crowd at a match is a British sporting usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The starting gate is the barrier from which horses are released at the start of a race.

clue.text: Boy's admitted defeat when 'e's lost

indicators.note: the letter e is named and taken away from the phrase before it

parts.note: to admit defeat is to give in, past tense gave in

explanation.surface: A lad conceded defeat once he found he had lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'e's' looks like Cockney for 'he's', but it names the letter E, which comes out of GAVE IN to leave GAVIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Gavin is a boy's first name.

clue.text: Helping porter in the grounds

parts.note: a helping is a portion, a ration of food
porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale

explanation.surface: A serving of dark beer is offered out in the grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' looks like a doorman, but it is the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the reasoning behind something, the grounds or basis for it.

clue.text: Aid for accessing communications that is usually dear?

definitions.meaning: a knife-like tool for slitting envelopes to get at mail
the first word of most correspondence is 'Dear', its usual opening

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a pun: the thing that opens a letter is usually the word 'Dear'.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter opener is a blade for slitting envelopes; and the greeting at the start of mail is also its opener.

clue.text: Police duties in uniform? By no means

definitions.meaning: an officer's patch is their beat
something not uniform at all, a mixture of odd pieces

explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' suggests police dress, but means all the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Patchwork is needlework of mismatched pieces, anything but uniform.

clue.text: Emergency help to make tree steady

parts.note: a fir is a kind of tree
staid means sober and steady

explanation.surface: A first responder props up a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: First aid is the immediate treatment given to an injured person.

clue.text: Heartlessly frightening songbird

indicators.note: without its heart means the central letter is removed

parts.note: startling means frightening or alarming

explanation.surface: A cruel scare is given to a songbird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartlessly' looks like cruelty, but removes the middle T of STARTLING.
explanation.definitionFit: The starling is a common speckled songbird.

clue.text: At home I scoffed, having called in to make peace

indicators.note: in shows the word for called is put inside the rest

parts.note: at home means in
to scoff food is to eat it greedily, past tense ate
termed means called or named

explanation.surface: Someone eating at home is asked to step in and settle a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make peace' is a verb here: intermediate as a verb is a rare word for mediate.
explanation.definitionFit: To intermediate is to mediate, to step in between parties to settle a dispute.

clue.text: It's too bad king has a separate state

parts.note: alas is a cry of regret, it's too bad
K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: Sadly a king rules a breakaway state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'separate' fits because Alaska is cut off from the other mainland states.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaska is a US state detached from the contiguous forty-eight by Canada.

clue.text: One'S not batted without concern

parts.note: reads like a cricketer kept out of the batting order, but alludes to the idiom that a calm person does not bat this

explanation.walkthrough: 'batted' suggests cricket; the idiom is 'not bat an eyelid', show no alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A cool person does not bat an eyelid, a fold of skin over the eye, when worried.

clue.text: Son markedly growing, becoming young man

parts.note: something tripling is increasing threefold, growing markedly

explanation.surface: A boy grows noticeably as he becomes a young man.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripling is a youth, a lad not yet fully grown.

clue.text: Essentially quiet language

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical abbreviation for quiet
Erse is a name for Scottish or Irish Gaelic

explanation.surface: At heart a language that is very quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Per se is Latin for in itself, intrinsically or essentially.

clue.text: Decoration for festival left in sacred place

indicators.note: in says the letter for left goes inside the word for sacred

parts.note: sacred means holy, as in a holy place

explanation.surface: Ornaments for a celebration are left in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprigs of holly are a traditional Christmas decoration.

clue.text: Building with many wings

parts.note: reads like a large mansion with many extensions, but means a structure housing lots of birds

explanation.walkthrough: 'wings' suggests the wings of a great house; here they belong to birds.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviary is an enclosure or house where many birds are kept.

clue.text: Where our case may appear before long?

definitions.text: Where our case may appear before long?

indicators.note: before puts the shuffled letters ahead of the letter for long
may appear suggests the words our case come out in a new form

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for long, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: An airline passenger waits for the luggage to show up soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may appear' rearranges the two words into CAROUSE, and 'before' sets that ahead of the letter for long; the whole clue also describes the airport belt.
explanation.definitionFit: A baggage carousel is the rotating belt at an airport where a traveller's suitcase turns up.

clue.text: Pursued with considerable tenacity

definitions.meaning: followed closely, tracked like a hound
persistently, stubbornly refusing to give up

explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them; and dogged means stubbornly persistent.

clue.text: Sailor has two lots of cards

parts.note: a deck is a full pack of cards
a hand is the set of cards dealt to one player

explanation.surface: A seaman is holding two sets of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A deckhand is a crew member who works on a ship's deck.
